record.paper_title: Mathematical contributions to the dynamics of the Josephson junctions: state of the art and open problems
record.original_question: For more physically significant Josephson-junction models, can the existing estimates and analysis be extended to the applied-magnetic-field equation ε u_xxt + u_xx − u_tt − a u_t = sin(u) − γ − b cos(kx), and to microshort or related variants such as ε u_xxt + u_xx − u_tt − a u_t = [1 − δ(x) μ] sin(u) − γ − b cos(kx), including cases where a gap in the vacuum chamber is considered? Here b represents an applied magnetic field parallel to the dielectric barrier plane, γ is the normalized current bias, and μ is the current density associated with the microshort.

evidence.quote: In some cases, extra terms must be considered. For example in a semiannular or in a S-shaped Josephson junction, when an applied magnetic field b parallel to the plane of the dielectric barrier is considered, the dynamic equation is: (1.3) εuxxt + uxx − utt − aut = sin u − γ − b cos(kx) where the last term evaluates a transient force on the trapped fluxons and locates these ones at the centre of the junction.

Moreover, if an annular junction, also provided with a microshort, is considered, the vortex dynamics in a static magnetic field is modelled with the general perturbed sine-Gordon equation (see,f.i. [7]): (1.4) εuxxt + uxx − utt − aut = [1 − δ(x)µ] sin u − γ − b cos(kx) where µ is the current density associated with the microshort.

Of course, in order to achieve estimates for other more significant physical problems, this analysis and many other estimates could be carried out for solution of equation (1.3) and for equations like (1.4) where the presence of a gap in the vacuum chamber is considered,too [37]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the perturbed sine-Gordon equation modelling fluxon dynamics in a Josephson junction subject to an applied magnetic field parallel to the plane of the dielectric barrier:

(A)  ε u_{xxt} + u_{xx} − u_{tt} − a u_t = sin(u) − γ − b cos(k x),

posed for (x,t) ∈ (0,L) × (0,∞), with prescribed initial data u(x,0), u_t(x,0) and suitable boundary conditions at x = 0, L. Here ε > 0 is a small dissipative parameter, a > 0 is a normal-current dissipation coefficient, γ ∈ ℝ is the normalized bias current, b ∈ ℝ represents the magnitude of an applied magnetic field parallel to the dielectric barrier, and k > 0 is a wavenumber.

Consider also the microshort/annular variant

(B)  ε u_{xxt} + u_{xx} − u_{tt} − a u_t = [1 − δ(x) μ] sin(u) − γ − b cos(k x),

where δ(x) is the Dirac distribution at a point representing a localized microshort and μ ∈ ℝ is the current density associated with that microshort, possibly together with the presence of a gap in the vacuum chamber (modelled by an additional spatial discontinuity in the coefficients).

Questions:
(i) Establish well-posedness (existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence on data) for classical or weak solutions of equations (A) and (B) in suitable functional spaces.
(ii) Derive a priori energy-type estimates and pointwise/asymptotic-in-time bounds for the solution u and its derivatives in terms of ε, a, γ, b, k, μ and the data, analogous to those known for the standard perturbed sine-Gordon equation ε u_{xxt} + u_{xx} − u_{tt} − a u_t = sin(u) − γ.
(iii) Analyze the singular limit ε → 0⁺ and obtain uniform-in-ε estimates for both (A) and (B), including the case in which a gap in the vacuum chamber is incorporated into the model.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem aiming to extend prior estimates for the basic perturbed sine-Gordon model to richer Josephson-junction equations including an applied magnetic field term and microshort/gap variants. Searches do not reveal a comprehensive resolution of well-posedness and uniform estimates for these specific equations; partial results exist for the simpler perturbed sine-Gordon equation but the extensions requested appear to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical contributions to the dynamics of the Josephson junctions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including extending estimates to equations with applied magnetic field and microshort terms.
status_evidence.claim: The extension of existing estimates to equations (A) and (B) is stated as an open direction.
